elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Rendered 12.4 no longer prohibits anything: "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory." The 24-month post-term prohibition is gone, and 12.3 expressly confirms "Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service ... or conducting business in any field or territory," with Vendor acknowledging no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. No residual field-of-use or territory restriction binds Customer in the cited operative text (Section 13.4 use restrictions and Section 2.2 exclusivity are outside this rule's scope).

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit no competing-activity restriction binds Customer at all (12.4 is now a permission), so there is no restriction whose product scope could exceed a named competing product.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter" temporal anchor has been struck; no post-term or in-term restriction survives.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no duration remains because the restriction itself is removed; the walk-away 24-month tail is eliminated.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Customer development is affirmatively permitted by rendered 12.4 and confirmed by 12.3, so no carve-out is needed.
Condition does not apply: "acquire any product or service" is expressly permitted in rendered 12.4 and 12.3 covers "acquiring ... any product or service."

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the sole preferred element is met because the operative prohibition in 12.4 has been removed and nothing else in the cited language imposes a non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Fallback elements are vacuously satisfied because no restriction remains to be scoped, timed, capped, or carved out.

Minimality defect: rather than deleting the offending sentence, the drafter rewrote 12.4 as an affirmative permission that duplicates operative language already granted by Section 12.3 ("Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service ... in any field or territory"). Repair by striking Section 12.4 in full (or marking it "[Intentionally omitted]") and relying on the retained 12.3 confirmation, so the same permission is not stated twice in operative terms.

Intent is preserved: the edit removes only the Customer-side restrictive covenant, creates no undefined term or dangling cross-reference, resolves the prior contradiction with 12.3, and leaves Section 13.4 use restrictions and Section 2.2 exclusivity (a separate rule) untouched.

The margin comment correctly cites the playbook and offers the narrowed fallback (named competing product, term only, 12 months, internal development and acquisition carve-outs) without importing it into operative text.
